doc.title: Bob Wilber interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 22, 1998

title: Benny Goodman as first love and influence
summary: Wilber grew up in the big band era; Goodman was the true King of Swing and his first great influence.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: It’s a pleasure to speak to you. And last night I was watching a video that you are in with a big band. And you were saying that your first love was big band, but your career started just a tad late.

Yeah, well I grew up, I was 70 in March so in the late ‘30s and early ‘40s of course that was the big band era and the music was in the air, it was on the radio all the time, and that was my first love, particularly on clarinet was certainly Benny Goodman, who was truly the “King of Swing,” I mean he just really was, it just wasn’t a name.
No. When they called Paul Whiteman the “King of Jazz” in the ‘20s, that was a platitude. But Benny Goodman was the “King of Swing.” He was certainly my first great influence.
